additions.reason: Central concept: the burial place of the tzaddik possesses the holiness of Eretz Yisrael. Eretz Yisrael is the dominant node connecting the tzaddik's grave and tikkun habrit.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁמְּקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The burial place of true tzaddikim is identified as having the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — a bechina relationship (shared essential nature: kedusha of the Land).
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים אֲמִתִּיִּים יוֹרְשִׁים אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁזּוֹכִין שֶׁמְּקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: Eretz Yisrael is stated to be a great tikkun for pgam habrit — this is a bechina-style identification (Eretz Yisrael IS tikkun for this), not merely a causal eitza.
additions.source_quote: וְאֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא תִּקּוּן גָּדוֹל לִפְגַם הַבְּרִית

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: ארץ ישראל — Eretz Yisrael, the Land of Israel, whose holiness is present at the tzaddik's grave
מקום גניזת הצדיקים — the burial place of true tzaddikim, identified with Eretz Yisrael's holiness
תיקון פגם הברית — rectification of the blemish of the covenant, for which Eretz Yisrael serves as a great tikkun
קבר הבעל שם טוב — the grave of the Baal Shem Tov, the specific instance motivating the teaching (may be too specific for a node)
